precepts.text: Solomon said, I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. That means all kind of sin. I'm showing you when Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.
precepts.point: Ahijah caught the new garment that was on Jeroboam and rent it in 12 pieces. Imagine you got a new garment on and somebody just start ripping pieces off. What the hell is this? Take thee ten pieces: I'm going to give you 10 tribes. That's the northern kingdom. But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. What happened? Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They did not all serve the same god: Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice; some involved sexual orgies. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods.

Solomon said it himself: “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.” Madness and folly means all kind of sin. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. When Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”, but “Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.” That is why Ahijah tore Jeroboam’s new garment into twelve pieces and told him to take ten: the northern kingdom, while one tribe was kept for David’s sake. That is the tabernacle of David that fell.

precepts.text: Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe: for we are the children of the prophets. Our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children. Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble.
precepts.point: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and built high places for Chemosh and for Molech, and did likewise for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
“But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh”. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because you are taking foreign women. We know it will turn your heart away from following the Lord, but what does it do to your brother? It says you hate your brother. Tobit shows it.

“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. He calls interracial marriage whoredom. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them”. Don’t despise your brethren. Passing over the daughters of your own people for strange women is despising your brethren in your heart. “for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.”

That is exactly where Solomon went. The Lord had said of those nations, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and Solomon clave unto them in love. His wives turned away his heart after Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh and Molech, and he built high places for them and for all his strange wives. That is how syncretism enters: through the strange wife, and it begins by despising your own people.

precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon? There is a book called the acts of Solomon, full of the spring of wisdom, things Solomon revealed that the Lord did not want us to know today.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?” So there is a book called the acts of Solomon, and we don't have it today. I would love to read that book.

Some of those books are full of what Ezra was told of the seventy: “For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.” Things Solomon revealed there, the Lord likely did not want us to know today, so he made it that we don't have possession of those books now.

That is also why the other books out there are left alone: Enoch, Jasher, the letter of Thomas and all that crazy stuff. This is warfare. Evil communication will corrupt you. You go reading that and certain thoughts start coming to your mind, and where did those thoughts come from? From that book you read. If you think you are strong enough to read it, that's on you, but it could confuse you. I'm going to stay with what the Lord gave us.

precepts.text: Rehoboam was the foolishness of the people, and Jeroboam showed Ephraim the way of sin.
precepts.point: The prophet Ahijah tore Jeroboam's garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten. God would take ten tribes from Solomon's son and leave one tribe for David's sake.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Solomon fell in love with heathen women, the very nations of which the Lord said “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and they did. He built a high place for Chemosh for his Moabite wife and for Molech for his Ammonite wife, and did the same for all his strange wives. So the Lord was angry with Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah “rent it in twelve pieces” and told Jeroboam, “Take thee ten pieces”: the kingdom would be rent out of the hand of Solomon’s son, with one tribe left for David’s sake.

Sirach sums up what Solomon left behind him when he died: “Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel.” Rehoboam was an idiot. He did not listen to the elders; he listened to the friends he grew up with, and by his counsel he turned the people away.

“There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin”. Jeroboam, the mighty man of valor Solomon made ruler over the house of Joseph, plotted against Solomon to rush the prophecy, fled to Egypt, and came back to take the ten tribes. And he showed Ephraim the way of sin.

So the heart Solomon gave to his strange wives bore its fruit in the next generation: a foolish son on the throne of Judah, a king who led Ephraim into sin, and the kingdom divided in two. That is where the dividing hatred between the houses begins.

precepts.text: When Solomon was old his strange wives turned away his heart, and he built an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab; the scripture shows numerous times that Chemosh was the god of the Moabites.
precepts.point: Naomi said, Thy sister in law is gone back unto her people and unto her gods. Those gods were idols; Chemosh was the god the Moabites served.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
The scripture shows numerous times that Chemosh was the god of the Moabites. “For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.” Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and did evil in the sight of the Lord.

“Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.” Chemosh is the abomination of Moab. His strange wives turned Solomon's heart to it; and those same gods of Moab are what Orpah returned to when she left Naomi.

precepts.text: Make no marriages with the other nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High.
precepts.point: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Make no marriages with the other nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High.

Solomon loved “women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites”, the very nations of which the Most High said, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”. It was not a maybe but a will. “Solomon clave unto these in love”, and “his wives turned away his heart.” It happened exactly as the Most High said it would.

precepts.text: Their daughters will go a whoring after their gods and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.
precepts.point: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.”

The law warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and Solomon is the proof. He had strange wives of the nations, and “his wives turned away his heart.” Their daughters went a whoring after their gods and made the king go a whoring after them too.

precepts.text: The king shall not multiply wives to himself, nor greatly multiply silver and gold, which is exactly what Solomon did.
precepts.point: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away: neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.”

That is exactly what Solomon did. “And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.” The law told the king why not to multiply wives, “that his heart turn not away”, and it turned away just as it said.

precepts.text: Israel bore the tabernacle of Molech and the star of their god, the six-pointed star that came from the idolatry of Solomon's day.
precepts.point: Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Israel bore the tabernacle of Molech and the star of their god, and that six-pointed star came from the idolatry of Solomon's day.

When Solomon was old, “his wives turned away his heart after other gods”, and he built “an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab”, “and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.” The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol. It has nothing to do with righteousness.

David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin. That is why Solomon's heart “was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father”, for a righteous man falls seven times and rises again.

precepts.text: Israel was still carrying the star of Remphan in the time of the apostles, the same idol.
precepts.point: Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.”

Israel was still carrying the star of Remphan in the time of the apostles. It is the same idol, the star of Molech that Solomon built a high place for, “figures which ye made to worship them”. What Solomon brought in for his strange wives, Israel carried on for generations, and the Most High answered it with captivity.

precepts.text: The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim.
precepts.point: The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim”. So when Solomon, “seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph”, Jeroboam was set over two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh.

Jeroboam the son of Nebat was “a mighty man of valour”, and he lifted up his hand against the king. The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him in the way, rent his new garment in twelve pieces, and said, “Take thee ten pieces”. The Most High would rend ten tribes out of Solomon's hand and give them to Jeroboam, leaving one tribe “for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake”. The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, and the ten tribes went to Jeroboam.

precepts.text: David charged Solomon to be strong, show himself a man, and keep the statutes of the Most High as written in the law of Moses.
precepts.point: The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
David charged Solomon before he died: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses”. The promise hung on it: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

Solomon did not keep that charge. The kingdom was rent “Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways”, “as did David his father.”

The same charge was then set before Jeroboam: “if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do that is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David”. Solomon sought to kill him, and Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

precepts.text: Solomon's wives turned his heart after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians.
precepts.point: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
Ahab followed the same road Solomon went down: “when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods”, and “Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians”.

Ahab took to wife “Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.” The Zidonians again. Solomon’s heart was turned by his wives, and Ahab’s was turned by his, until he reared up an altar for Baal and made a grove, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger more than all the kings of Israel before him.

precepts.text: In his old age Solomon went after Ashtoreth, Milcom, and Chemosh and built high places for these abominations, the corruption Josiah now tore down.
precepts.point: This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.” He “went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father. Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.”

In his old age Solomon built these high places, and they stood until Josiah: “the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile.”

Josiah tore down the corruption Solomon began. He broke the images, cut down the groves and filled their places with the bones of men. This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and fall under punishment.

precepts.text: The Lord, angry that Solomon's heart turned to other gods, declares he will rend the kingdom from him and give it to his servant; this is the prophecy now being fulfilled.
precepts.point: The king does not listen to the people, for the cause was of the Most High, that the Lord might fulfill the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 10: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders and the Kingdom Divides

precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice.” He had commanded Solomon “that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.”

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.” That is the prophecy now being fulfilled. When Rehoboam answered the people roughly and hearkened not unto them, “the cause was of God, that the Lord might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.”

precepts.text: Jeroboam, Solomon's industrious servant, lifts his hand against the king, and the prophet Ahijah tears his garment in twelve pieces and gives him ten tribes.
precepts.point: He names Jeroboam as the servant of Solomon who rose up and rebelled against his lord. To understand that rebellion, the account goes back to 1 Kings 11.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
Abijah names Jeroboam as “the servant of Solomon the son of David” who “is risen up, and hath rebelled against his lord.” To understand that rebellion, go back to 1 Kings 11: “Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant … even he lifted up his hand against the king.”

He was industrious: “the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valour: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.”

Then the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the field, took the new garment, “and rent it in twelve pieces: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee.”

Against that, Abijah stands on mount Zemaraim and declares that “the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt.”

precepts.text: Solomon loved many strange women, and when he was old his wives turned away his heart after other gods, exactly as the law warned they would.
precepts.point: Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah asked, “Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things?” Here is the record: “But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites; Of the nations concerning which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.”

He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and “when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.” Exactly as the law warned, the strange women turned away his heart.

Among many nations there was no king like Solomon, beloved of his God, and even him did outlandish women cause to sin. If it happened to him, the men of Judah marrying wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab had no ground to think it would not happen to them.

precepts.text: Solomon's wives turned his heart after other gods, beginning the idolatry that led to the kingdom's division.
precepts.point: Isaiah is a heavy, prophetic book; even the Ethiopian eunuch was reading Isaiah when the spirit sent Philip to help him understand it.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

precepts.why:
Isaiah’s vision concerns “Judah and Jerusalem”, the southern kingdom. By his day the split between the northern and southern kingdoms had already come, and it goes back to Solomon’s idolatry. “For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.”

Solomon’s wives turned his heart after other gods. That idolatry is what led to the kingdom’s division, and to Isaiah prophesying to Judah and Jerusalem apart from the north.

precepts.text: Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, the tribal god also known as Molech or Malcham.
precepts.point: But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god which ye made to yourselves. This was going on even during the time of Solomon.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” This was going on even during the time of Solomon: “Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.” Milcom, the tribal god of the Ammonites, is also known as Molech or Malcham, the Moloch whose tabernacle Israel bore.

Instead of judgment running down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream, the house of Israel carried the god of the Ammonites, even in Solomon's day.

Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice.

Being that Solomon was into it, the navy was involved in it; that is the reason you see those symbols in some of the records of the people that came over. But that is not a symbol we are supposed to be dealing with. It is not the Star of David; that is not in the Bible.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

points: King Solomon loved many strange women, of the nations concerning which the Lord said, ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because he is taking foreign women.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and built high places for Chemosh and for Molech, and did likewise for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: Solomon loved many strange women, and they turned his heart to other gods. He built high places for Chemosh and Molech for his Moabite and Ammonite wives.
The prophet Ahijah tore Jeroboam's garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten. God would take ten tribes from Solomon's son and leave one tribe for David's sake.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Solomon loved many strange women besides the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites, nations the Most High had said Israel should not join with, for surely they would turn their heart after their gods; and Solomon clave to these in love.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: When Solomon was old his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Most High as David his father's was; he went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and did evil in the sight of the Most High.
David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin; this is why a righteous man falls seven times and rises again.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The Most High was angry with Solomon because his heart was turned from him who had appeared to him twice and commanded him not to go after other gods, but he kept not the commandment.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Therefore the Most High said he would surely rend the kingdom from Solomon and give it to his servant, but not in Solomon's days for David's sake; he would rend it out of the hand of his son.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: This is the pivotal moment in the history of Israel, for this sin divided the kingdom under Jeroboam and Rehoboam. The Most High said he would not rend all the kingdom but would give one tribe to the son of David for David's sake and for Jerusalem's sake.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The Most High stirred up an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of the king's seed in Edom, for when David was in Edom, Joab remained six months until he had cut off every male, and Hadad fled as a child to Egypt where Pharaoh gave him favor, a house, and a wife.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Esau was always the first hater and enemy of Israel, comforting himself in the thought of killing us. When Hadad heard David and Joab were dead, he sought to return to his own country.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The Most High also stirred up Rezin the son of Eliadah, who gathered men, reigned in Damascus, and was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon. There was peace under Solomon while he kept the commandments, but when he broke them the Most High gave strength to his enemies.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant, a mighty man of valor, lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon had made him ruler over the charge of the house of Joseph, which was the two tribes Ephraim and Manasseh.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam in the way, took his new garment, rent it in twelve pieces, and gave Jeroboam ten, saying the Most High would rend ten tribes from Solomon's hand and give them to him. One tribe would remain for David's servant's sake and for Jerusalem, because Israel had forsaken the Most High and worshipped Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

points: The rest of the acts of Solomon and his wisdom are written in the book of the acts of Solomon; he reigned in Jerusalem over Israel forty years, then slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.
